item.title: Trump says anyone who does not refer to AI as ‘super intelligence’ is ‘THE ENEMY'
Trump decrees that anyone who uses the term Artificial Intelligence is now ‘The Enemy!’
item.description:
## Top Stories: President Donald Trump on Thursday opened up a new front in his ongoing war against commonly used terms and geographic names by warning that anyone referring to Large Language Models such as OpenAI's ChatGPT or Anthropic's Claude as "Artificial Intelligence" would earn themselves a place on his enemies list.
The president's outburst-cum-veiled threat landed just over a week after he signed an executive order directing executive branch agencies to begin referring to artificial intelligence, which is now embedded across the federal government, as "super intelligence" following a lunch [with leaders in the AI industry,](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/trump-ai-meeting-elon-musk-jeff-bezos-b3058451.html) including Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, Dario Amodei and others.

item.title: Anthropic’s artificial intelligence gave a false homicide tip to Philly police, triggering a meeting with the company
item.description:
# Anthropic’s artificial intelligence gave a false homicide tip to Philly police, triggering a meeting with the company The Anthropic Claude logo on a laptop on Aug. 22, 2025. Read moreGabby Jones / Bloomberg
ET
Listen to article •0:00 min
An artificial intelligence model operated by Anthropic submitted false information about an unsolved Philadelphia homicide to the police department’s public tip forum this summer, law enforcement officials said Friday.
The unprecedented incident occurred in July and raised concern among department leaders, who met with Anthropic representatives to discuss the interaction on Thursday, police said.
Eric Gripp, a police spokesperson, said an Anthropic AI model contactedthe department’s tip forum, PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, around 11:30 p.m. on July 18.
The model gave information purporting to come from someone with information about an unsolved homicide, he said.
Anthropic told police the false tip was generated as the company tested interactions between its AI model and “randomly selected websites,” according to Gripp.
The company discovered the error on Sept. 28.
A little more than a week earlier, authorities said, Philadelphia police received the artificially generated homicide tip.
